testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, when should you shift into a lower gear?

options.text: Before you start going down the hill
After you have started going down the hill
As far down the hill as possible
At the bottom of the hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going down the hill
questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before you start going down a hill. This helps you control your speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle
To stop the vehicle during normal driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle
questions.explanation: Use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: How do you remove water and oil from an air storage tank?

options.text: Siphon the water and oil out of the tank
Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil
The water and oil drain out automatically when the brakes are used
Use a sponge to soak up the water and oil

questions.correctAnswerText: Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil
questions.explanation: Water and oil are removed from air storage tanks through a drain valve. If left in the tank, they can damage the brakes. Tanks must be drained manually every day to prevent buildup.

questions.question: What is the name of a thin layer of ice on road surfaces?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may look wet. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Where can you find the tire load rating?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating shows the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: Why is backing up with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle
Most trucks cannot move in reverse
Cargo may fall out of the trailer
There may be extra weight in the front of the trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you must back up, use a helper if possible.

questions.question: What should you do when checking your vehicle's lights before driving?

options.text: Keep the engine running and the vehicle in gear
Check the lights from inside the vehicle
Check the lights using the reflection from a shiny surface

questions.explanation: To check your lights, set the parking brake, turn off the engine, and remove the key. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Exit the vehicle and check that all lights are working.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, when can you exit your vehicle to check its position?

options.text: You are not allowed to exit the vehicle
You are discouraged from exiting the vehicle
Only if the vehicle is in reverse
Only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set
questions.explanation: Put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before exiting during the test. You can check the vehicle's position a maximum of twice, except for straight line backing, where you can look only once.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a header board?

options.text: They protect the driver from cargo hitting them
They protect the driver's head when entering the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect the driver from cargo hitting them
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo shifts forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: What condition should engine belts be in?
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. The correct amount of slack varies by vehicle, so learn what is right for your vehicle.

questions.question: During an inspection, your brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, check for cracked drums and shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them. Also look for shoes that are missing, broken, or too thin.

questions.question: If you don't secure a load on a flatbed trailer, the cargo may:

options.text: Shift or fall off the trailer.
Create a glare that blinds other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift or fall off the trailer.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, you must secure cargo to prevent it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Quickly swerve into the other lane.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal when changing lanes. Make sure there is enough space for your entire vehicle in the next lane before you move.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes your vehicle stop in a shorter distance.
Reduces the time it takes for brakes to work.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up during hard braking. This gives you better control. However, it does not always make your vehicle stop in a shorter distance.

questions.question: During driving exercises other than the straight line backing exercise, how many pull-ups are allowed without a penalty?
questions.explanation: You are allowed two pull-ups without penalty during most skills test exercises. The straight line backing exercise allows only one pull-up. Using more than the allowed number of pull-ups in a single exercise will result in failing the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: Bent lock rings:
questions.explanation: Do not use lock rings that are mismatched, bent, or cracked. They are dangerous.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle as the engine nears idle speed, you should:
questions.explanation: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch as the engine nears idle speed.

questions.question: After finishing a trip, you should:

options.text: Take the vehicle out of service.

questions.explanation: After each trip, you may need to inspect the vehicle you drove and file a report on its condition.

questions.question: When checking underneath your vehicle for leaks, look for all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before a trip, look underneath your vehicle for leaks of fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery when rain first starts to fall?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Fresh rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road surface to create a slick film. As rain continues, this mixture eventually washes away.

questions.question: If you are pulled over on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Use the taillights to warn other drivers.
Keep your lights off so you do not distract other drivers.
Place items from your vehicle on the road to warn drivers.

questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers and use warning signals to alert other drivers.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth required on the main grooves of a front tire?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in the main grooves. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: How should cargo be secured on a flatbed trailer?
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to stop it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following is NOT required?

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. You must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without accidents or violations.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, parking brakes are controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to set the parking brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the on-road driving test, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily while in the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily while in the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions and slow down before entering. Keep your vehicle in its lane and continue checking traffic. Do not brake steadily throughout the curve; brake before entering it.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers to alert other drivers.

questions.question: What is the name for a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice that lets you see the road beneath it. A road covered in black ice looks wet. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road appears wet.

questions.question: When backing up, what is the best practice?

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side whenever possible.

questions.explanation: When backing up, go slowly and use mirrors on both sides of your vehicle. Use a helper to watch your blind spots when possible. You and the helper should agree on a signal to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Do not signal if you think others already know what you plan to do.
Cancel your signal after the turn is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not signal if you think others already know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal whenever you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think others know your intentions. Signal early, signal throughout the turn, and cancel the signal when you finish turning.

questions.question: Always drive so you can stop your vehicle:

options.text: Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive so your vehicle can stop completely within the area of road you can see in front of you.

questions.question: The most common foundation brake is the:
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What is another name for front end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called headache racks. They protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Never use the brake pedal if spring brakes are on. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: In Illinois, what is the weight limit for a five-axle combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: In Illinois, five-axle combination vehicles can weigh up to 80,000 pounds on state and local roads. The maximum weight allowed depends on how far apart the axles are.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Move all wheels onto the shoulder.
Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
Stay on the shoulder until the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely before returning to the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you drive onto the shoulder, try to keep one set of wheels on the road for better control. Stop completely on the shoulder if you can, then return to the road when safe.

questions.question: Slippery roads usually:

options.text: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to drive a vehicle.
Can be avoided by driving at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Drive carefully when conditions could make the road slippery.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Exit the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to remove the vehicle.
Walk down the tracks to look for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle right away and walk away from the tracks. Contact emergency services.

questions.question: A CDL holder who leaves the scene of an accident will have their license disqualified for:
questions.explanation: Leaving the scene of an accident will result in license disqualification for at least 12 months.

questions.question: Before looking under your vehicle's hood, you should:

options.text: Use parking brakes and/or chock blocks.
Leave the vehicle in a low gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use parking brakes and/or chock blocks.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting under the hood, engage the parking brake and/or block the wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: What happens if a vehicle's engine runs without oil?

options.text: The vehicle will jerk while driving.
The engine may be damaged quickly.
The vehicle will use less gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine may be damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine can break down fast without oil. If your oil pressure gauge shows low or changes often, do not drive the vehicle.

questions.question: Good drivers look ____ seconds ahead of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead on the road. This gives you time to react to dangers before you reach them.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Let rain water enter air tanks.
Remove water and oil from air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have drains in the air tanks to remove water and oil. If these build up, they can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: Cargo 40 feet long on a flatbed trailer must have at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo on flatbed trailers. You need at least two tie-downs no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil in an air brake system should be:

options.text: Added if they are needed for the system to work.
Added if the level is low.
Left alone—they are not a problem.

questions.explanation: Water and oil build up in air brake systems and can damage the brakes. Open air tank drains manually each day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Why should you be careful around rental trucks?

options.text: Drivers are worried about their cargo.
Drivers may not know about the poor views on the sides and back.
They do not handle like other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may not know about the poor views on the sides and back.
questions.explanation: Rental truck drivers may not be used to vehicles with limited side and rear views. Drivers who cannot see other vehicles are dangerous.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The lightest safe weight a tire can carry
The heaviest safe weight a tire can carry
How much the tire itself weighs
The weight of air in a fully inflated tire

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a set pressure. This information is printed on the tire's side.

questions.question: When making a turn, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to signal other drivers.
Turn off your signal before turning to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.explanation: Signal before you turn so drivers behind you know your plans. Keep your signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is done.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly, you should:
questions.explanation: If you drive slowly, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers, where local law allows this.

questions.question: In a convex mirror, objects look ____ than they really are.
questions.explanation: A convex mirror makes objects look smaller and farther away than they actually are.
